name: Evaluate RBS
description: You are given $$$2n$$$ tuples of values $$$(a, b, c)$$$, where $$$a$$$ and $$$b$$$ are positive integers and $$$c$$$ is a bracket ' ( ' or ' ) '. Exactly $$$n$$$ tuples have $$$c = $$$' ( ' and the other $$$n$$$ tuples have $$$c =$$$ ' ) '. You are asked to choose two positive values $$$x$$$ and $$$y$$$ ($$$x \gt 0$$$ and $$$y \gt 0$$$; not necessarily integers ) and sort the tuples in the increasing value of $$$a \cdot x + b \cdot y$$$. If several tuples have the same value, you can place them in any order among themselves. Is it possible to choose such $$$x$$$ and $$$y$$$ that taking brackets $$$c$$$ from the tuples in the resulting order produces a regular bracket sequence? A regular bracket sequence is a bracket sequence that can be transformed into a correct arithmetic expression by inserting characters " 1 " and " + " between the original characters of the sequence.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 1500$$$) — the number of testcases. The first line of each testcase contains a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 1500$$$). The $$$i$$$-th of the next $$$2n$$$ lines contains two integers $$$a_i$$$ and $$$b_i$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i, b_i \le 10^6$$$) and a character $$$c_i$$$ ($$$c_i = $$$' ( ' or $$$c_i = $$$' ) '). Exactly $$$n$$$ tuples have $$$c_i = $$$' ( ' and the other $$$n$$$ tuples have $$$c_i =$$$ ' ) '. The sum of $$$n$$$ over all testcases doesn't exceed $$$1500$$$.
output_specification: For each testcase, print " YES " if it's possible to choose such $$$x$$$ and $$$y$$$ that taking brackets $$$c$$$ from the tuples in the resulting order produces a regular bracket sequence. Otherwise, print " NO ".
subsubtopic: 480. Points, Vectors, Transformations, Dot Products, Cross Products, Precision Issues and Polar Sort(2D)
approach_summary: Apply Points, Vectors, Transformations, Dot Products, Cross Products, Precision Issues and Polar Sort(2D) paradigm under the Geometry framework. Exploit problem invariants to reduce state space and achieve optimal complexity.
